body.target_estimand: \(\mathcal P_{\mathrm{SI}}(\mathcal O)\) is the endpoint-invariance structural target over the note's finite-alphabet faithful shared-response compatibility fiber. On the separate fixed-\(A\) purely graphical fiber, the established result is \(\mathcal M_A^{\mathrm{gr}}(e)=\mathcal G_A(u,v;k)\). At law level, \(\varnothing\ne\mathcal M_A^{\mathrm{faith}}(e)\subseteq\mathcal M_A^{\mathrm{gr}}(e)\); singleton \(\mathcal G_A\) gives equality automatically, whereas two-mark equality requires nonempty faithful realization fibers. Equality of a fixed observable rule closure with \(\mathcal P_{\mathrm{SI}}(\mathcal O)\) remains a conditional implication requiring faithful realization and an unknown-\(A\) extension theorem.
body.estimand_functional: For \(e\in\mathcal E(\mathcal O)\), \(\mathcal P_{\mathrm{SI}}(\mathcal O)(e)=m\) if and only if \(\mu_\eta(e)=m\) for every \(\eta\in\mathcal C(\mathcal O)\), and \(\mathcal P_{\mathrm{SI}}(\mathcal O)(e)=\mathtt{circle}\) otherwise, where \(\mathcal C(\mathcal O)\) is formed inside the finite-alphabet, positive-selection, pooled-law-faithful shared-response subclass \(\mathfrak M_{D,K}^{\mathrm{Dai}}\) defined in this note, not the entire published graphical class.

sampling_model.design: Oracle graphical analysis uses the observational selected-law MAG signature and \(K\) pooled binary-indicator MAG signatures coupled by one model-specific basal selected DAG. The structural target is endpoint invariance over the note's finite-alphabet, positive-selection, pooled-law-faithful shared-response subclass; the established results are exact on a separate fixed-\(A\) graphical fiber and conditional at the unknown-\(A\) law level.
sampling_model.units: The primitive law-level object is \(\eta=(S_\eta,G_0(\eta),(T_k(\eta))_{k=1}^{K},(\kappa^{(j)}(\eta))_{j=0}^{K})\), generated by one shared-exogenous response-function family. At \(K=0\), its oracle law is \(P_{\eta}^{(0)}=\mathcal L_{\eta}(X\mid S_\eta^*=\mathbf1)\); for each \(k\in[K]\), the comparison uses the pooled law \(P_{\eta,k}^{\mathrm{pool}}\) on \(X\cup\{\zeta_k\}\).
sampling_model.treatment: Regime membership is observed. Each direct soft-intervention target set \(T_k(\eta)\) is latent and may differ from the indicator-neighbor set \(Z_k\), which can also contain indirectly affected ancestrally selected variables.
sampling_model.overlap: The common basal selection event \(S_\eta^*=\mathbf1\) has positive probability for every law-level model, so all selected and pooled oracle laws are defined.
sampling_model.nuisance_estimation: Not applicable to the proved oracle statements. No finite-sample conditional-independence or invariance tests, separation margin, or simultaneous error-control theorem is assumed or established.

body.tldr: Selection before perturbation couples every pooled regime through one basal selected DAG and one shared-response twin SCM. The proved structural result is the exact fixed-\(A\) graphical identity \(\mathcal M_A^{\mathrm{gr}}=\mathcal G_A\). At law level, the faithful mark set is nonempty and contained in that graphical set, so singleton graphical sets give equality automatically; two-mark faithful witnesses require nonempty realization fibers. For a directly coupled nonempty open rational parameter family supplied as an additional premise, simultaneous pooled faithfulness within that family is equivalent to atomic determinant nontriviality; neither the family nor the certificates are constructed here. Constructing the parameter family, proving the atomic certificates, finding a finite observable unknown-\(A\) extension, and establishing canonical endpoint equality remain open. The achieved result is therefore below a complete-calculus result. Neither faithful realization nor the unknown-\(A\) extension follows from graphical inclusion.

project_justification.gap: Dai et al.'s graphical endpoint semantics do not furnish two faithful representatives from one basal selected DAG and one coupled shared-response twin SCM. The law-level gap has two parts: for every admissible replacement, construct a directly coupled nonempty open rational parameter family satisfying all model conditions except possibly pooled twin faithfulness, and prove a nonzero cleared determinant for every \(m\)-connected query on that family. Separately, no finite observable unknown-\(A\) extension theorem synchronizes the common exterior completion across regimes. The parameter construction, atomic certificates, finite rule list, canonical equality, and separation-margin confidence result all remain open.
project_justification.niche: The note delivers the exact fixed-\(A\) structural characterization \(\mathcal M_A^{\mathrm{gr}}=\mathcal G_A\), then cleanly separates it from the nonempty faithful inclusion and from the open unknown-\(A\) problem. Singleton graphical mark sets identify the faithful endpoint, whereas a two-mark graphical set reaches law-level equality only when both required realization fibers are nonempty. This is a technical foundation below a complete-calculus result.
project_justification.fill: Explicit empty-graph and signature-monotone-path replacements establish the two graphical marks while preserving the full regime signatures. The faithful-model mark set is nonempty and lies inside the exact graphical set, giving automatic equality in singleton cases and only a conditional equality in the two-mark case. For a supplied directly coupled rational parameterization, the determinant proof shows that atomic nontriviality is sufficient and necessary for a common simultaneously faithful parameter. A separate conditional implication says that a supplied sound finite observable rule list with nonempty replacement realizations and opposing endpoint extensions has canonical endpoint closure; under an additional uniform premise-decidability condition, saturation makes at most \((K+1)D(D-1)\) strict reported-endpoint updates. Neither antecedent is a consequence of graphical inclusion.

body.related_work: Dai et al.'s Lemmas 3--6 provide the graphical twin-MAG interface for causally sufficient, childless pre-treatment selection, while their Theorem 3 establishes CDIS soundness and their discussion leaves completeness uncertain. The present note uses a finite-alphabet, positive-selection, pooled-law-faithful shared-response subclass of those graphical models and does not claim equality with Dai et al.'s full law class. Zhang's Sections 3--4 and Theorem 2 establish arrowhead and tail completeness for a single observational PAG, but not simultaneous common-basal pooled regimes. Ali, Richardson, and Spirtes provide single-MAG equivalence invariants that motivate full-signature preservation, not faithful common-basal realization. The public Zhou--Kocaoglu abstract concerns known-target completion with enumeration, which is excluded here as a headline calculus. Wang, Du, and Zhou inform computational context; the present computable statement is only the conditional bound of \((K+1)D(D-1)\) strict endpoint updates for a supplied fixed rule list. Jaber et al. treat unknown targets without selection, and Luo et al. concern a distinct post-treatment-selection setting. Relative to these comparators, the result is an exact fixed-\(A\) graphical theorem and a conditional law-level implication, not completeness.
body.technical_internal_limitation: The replacement construction specifies a selection set, basal DAG, and intervention targets, but no law-level coupling. The exceptional-set lemma now starts only after a nonempty open rational family of tuples is supplied directly, with one product exogenous law, the same realized vector across worlds, response functions shared off target, one basal selection response, positive selection probability, positive pooled cells, positive rational denominators, and the Markov direction. It adds pooled twin faithfulness when the atomic determinants are nontrivial; it does not construct that family or certify those determinants. The exact graphical identity does not imply two-mark faithful realization, and neither faithful realization nor graphical inclusion supplies a finite observable unknown-\(A\) extension. No separation margin or finite-sample testing theorem is supplied, so canonical equality and simultaneous confidence SI-PAGs remain open.
body.honest_scope: The proved structural content is the exact fixed-selection-ancestry identity \(\mathcal M_A^{\mathrm{gr}}=\mathcal G_A\) on the purely graphical Dai fiber. At law level, \(\varnothing\ne\mathcal M_A^{\mathrm{faith}}\subseteq\mathcal M_A^{\mathrm{gr}}\); singleton \(\mathcal G_A\) gives equality, while two-mark equality requires nonempty faithful realization fibers. The algebraic lemma is conditional on a supplied directly coupled nonempty open rational parameter family satisfying positivity and the Markov direction, plus one nonzero determinant certificate per \(m\)-connected query. Constructing the family, proving those certificates, producing opposing faithful two-mark witnesses, finding a finite observable unknown-\(A\) extension rule list, proving unconditional canonical equality, and deriving simultaneous finite-sample confidence guarantees are open. Neither the faithful-realization antecedent nor the unknown-\(A\) extension antecedent follows from graphical inclusion. Thus the result is below a complete-calculus result; a global basal-DAG enumerator is not offered as the headline method.
